decisions.reason: As a core airfield-control hardware extension with long industrial lifecycles, its value should now be clearer and the absence of negative evidence makes abandonment unlikely relative to the low benefit of keeping it in the portfolio.
The airport systems training program is a low-cost complementary service that supports the installed base and keeps a useful option open while adding little portfolio risk.

This narrower training course is somewhat easier to fold into broader offerings, but as a low-cost complement to core airfield lighting business it is still worth retaining unless demand clearly disappoints.
The collaboration software tool fits the firm’s move toward integrated, data-sharing airport operations, so despite adoption uncertainty its strategic upside justifies keeping the option alive.

The multilateration surveillance system is a flagship product aligned with the firm’s future direction, and although it is costlier to support than training offers, long airport procurement cycles favor continued commitment rather than early withdrawal.
